recommended_physical_target.name: Same-material NC finite-energy nonadiabatic force-response spectrum about the admitted loaded Ni31H6 background
recommended_physical_target.physical_object: The linear retarded electronic backreaction on the full coupled H/Ni displacement tangent, represented first in Cartesian perturbations and then projected onto admitted G1 coupled modes with their actual masses, phases and normalization. Preserve off-diagonal mode mixing; no H-only frozen-Ni reduction.
recommended_physical_target.material_model: The separately registered QE7.5 scalar-relativistic collinear spin-PBE SG15-2020 Ni18/H1 ordinary pseudo-space model. Use its own settled geometry, magnetic state, electronic states, operators and modes. No SOC, no selected-UPF NLCC, frozen Ni core and pseudo-observable limitations remain explicit.
recommended_physical_target.first_background_and_controls: Begin with loaded Ni31H6 only after the all-four NC prerequisite and L1 are satisfied. Pristine Ni32, empty-vacancy Ni31 and dispersed Ni32H6 remain matched G1 controls; their eventual response comparisons require their own electronic/vertex inputs. First loaded response alone is not a loading/defect/arrangement design ranking.
recommended_physical_target.momentum_and_frequency: Use a registered commensurate nonzero-q perturbation with a closed k to k+q electronic mapping and its conjugate partner. Resolve finite electronic transition energies across the actual admitted coupled-mode frequency range and a separately handled low-frequency sector. Gamma is a separate limit/control, not all finite-q response. Exact q member, frequency window and numerical resolutions are deferred to actual G1 modes and response registration, not guessed here.
recommended_physical_target.observable: Complex Cartesian/mode force-response matrix and its finite-energy electronic absorption contribution at actual mode energies, with raw real/imaginary/off-diagonal structure retained. A separately defined longitudinal pseudo-density susceptibility/dielectric-loss channel may accompany it. Report approximation-scoped spectral response, not a fitted lifetime, scalar universal friction or nuclear rate.
recommended_physical_target.screening_approximation: Prospective first approximation is the source-scoped KS independent-electron, static screened-vertex approximation behind Giustino Eq145, not the full dynamically screened Eq141. Explicit spin-PBE/nonlocal finite-q extension and its action/functional matching remain load-bearing dependencies; no blanket factor two or exact physical-force identification is imported from the spin-degenerate compact source formula.
recommended_physical_target.scientific_value: It can identify whether the actual coupled Ni/H modes encounter electronic absorption and nonadiabatic mixing within the declared model. Their magnitude, existence at particular mode energies, convergence and design consequence are not established by this specification.
recommended_physical_target.not_claimed: Neither all-electron/contact response nor physical transverse finite-q response, a complete thermal bath, irreversible damping, material coherence, many-region propagation, lattice-design superiority or a nuclear enhancement follows.

ensemble.reference_statics: Neutral fixed mean electron number at the declared physical FD temperature or its explicitly controlled zero-temperature limit. Fixed-mean-N Legendre curvature, fixed-mu grandcanonical curvature and exact finite canonical curvature are distinct; select the one represented by the material energy/free-energy calculation. Fixed mean N is not an exact canonical Fock state.
ensemble.dynamic_state: Isolated retarded response about the same stationary equilibrium electronic state, with occupations initially fixed by that state. This supplies no population relaxation law. Coupled spin/charge response and any fixed versus relaxed magnetization constraint must match the eventual static calculation and be stated in the response registration.
ensemble.numerical_vs_physical: Existing MV occupations/degauss are numerical integration choices. FD is a declared one-electron equilibrium model, not a measured temperature. Eta is a retarded prescription/integration regulator, not physical temperature or a fitted electron/phonon lifetime.

zero_frequency_and_degeneracy.retained_sector: Keep the complete zero-frequency occupation/degenerate-subspace covariance, including off-diagonal matrix elements within exactly degenerate blocks. Do not replace it by diagonal band-label fluctuations or discard it because the retarded commutator vanishes there.
zero_frequency_and_degeneracy.static_vs_dynamic: The isolated retarded zero-frequency response omits exactly degenerate transitions; the isothermal curvature includes the corresponding population sector. These are not interchangeable. Limits involving coalescing gaps, zero frequency, occupation temperature and population relaxation cannot be silently interchanged.
zero_frequency_and_degeneracy.representation: Block-covariant handling at degeneracies; equal equilibrium occupations within an exactly degenerate energy subspace in the cited quasi-free Gibbs setting. Zero-frequency covariance is a separate static sector, not a zero-gap thermal oscillator. No finite population relaxation time is supplied.
zero_frequency_and_degeneracy.consequence: If future dynamics needs equilibration of this sector, a separately sourced relaxation model and noise construction are missing physical inputs; do not create them with eta.

force_response_vs_transition_bath.force_vertex: The explicit ionic derivative at fixed electronic state contains the local term and both nonlocal projector sides. The screened KS displacement derivative additionally contains induced HXC. Raw Cartesian energy/length vertices are not yet mass/mode-normalized couplings; ion-ion and required second-order static terms are not exhausted by a first-order vertex product.
force_response_vs_transition_bath.selected_product: Use the cited mixed bare-times-screened self-energy structure with its own static subtraction. Preserve complete complex ordered contractions, spin channels, k/k+q correspondence and mode cross channels. Do not substitute a modulus square, Hermitize an inconvenient response, clip negative modes or force a mixed response into a positive oscillator bath.
force_response_vs_transition_bath.alternative_product: A screened-square independent-KS transition bath is a separately declared effective one-body coupling model. The admitted finite-fermion positive-gap map supports connected two-point response/noise only under its stated Gibbs/quasi-free conditions; it does not prove this alternative equals the material force self-energy or reproduces nonlinear/higher cumulant dynamics.
force_response_vs_transition_bath.source_boundary: Giustino Eq146 explicitly replaces the bare coupling by screened coupling. Eq185 additionally neglects finite phonon energy in the transition delta and takes a low-temperature limit. Neither replacement is selected for the first target; adequacy at eventual H-mode energies is unknown.

static_screening_subtraction.rule: Subtract only the electronic curvature already included in the calibrated ionic stiffness, under the same operators, screening approximation, ensemble, charge/spin constraints and action. The cited dynamic-minus-static expression is a source-defined matching structure, not permission to subtract any convenient zero-frequency number.
static_screening_subtraction.material_boundary: G1 Born-Oppenheimer force constants already include their declared static electronic response. Combining them with a full additional electronic bath/response without matched subtraction would double count. Conversely isolated retarded static subtraction is not generally the isothermal GC or fixed-mean-N curvature.
static_screening_subtraction.MV_mismatch: Current numerical-MV reference data do not by themselves provide the physical-FD fixed-mean-N counterterm. Require a registered common-limit justification or same-model static recalculation; do not fit a shift to restore desired mode frequencies. Preserve raw instabilities and uncertainties.
static_screening_subtraction.missing_construction: The actual material-level projected action and matching counterterm are not available here. Their future new-claim oracle must bind the chosen NC spin/nonlocal functional and constraints before any combined production response/dynamics claim.

dissipation_and_limits.included: Prospective electronic electron-hole absorption within the declared KS/screening approximation, resolved at finite transition energy; retain a finite spectral representation rather than infer irreversible damping from a smoothed plot.
dissipation_and_limits.not_supplied: Physical electron-electron/impurity collision rates, anharmonic phonon decay, defects/disorder scattering, spin relaxation, external reservoirs and their energy/noise balance. Omitted channels remain omitted; a single absorption channel is not the complete disposal of deposited energy.
dissipation_and_limits.finite_system: A finite retained electronic or oscillator bath has recurrences. Two-point Gaussian equivalence does not establish higher moments, nonlinearity, population thermalization or an irreversible lifetime.
dissipation_and_limits.numerical_limits: Register independent k/q sampling, occupied/unoccupied energy coverage, wavefunction/response cutoff, occupation-limit, frequency quadrature and eta refinements at fixed physical observable. Establish a resolved continuum/integration limit before interpreting absorption as a material linewidth; taking eta to zero on an unresolved finite list is not such a result.
dissipation_and_limits.physical_limits: Keep finite-q longitudinal, q approaching zero, optical tensor and finite-q transverse channels distinct. No transverse tensor from a longitudinal scalar response. Region-array size, material Brillouin-zone resolution and physical density are separate controls. No Markov limit or low-energy Fermi-surface reduction is assumed.
dissipation_and_limits.noise: Do not apply the finite-fermion same-operator FDT/bath map indiscriminately to the mixed-vertex force expression. A complete effective action with its correct observable/noise pairing is needed before a thermal G3 consumer.
